title: Escaping the Self-Repair Trap: Improving Test Oracle Generation via Dual-Context Awareness
abstract: arXiv:2608.05917v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for regression-oracle completion, where a test prefix is given and the current program version is treated as expected behavior. Recent approaches increasingly rely on iterative self-repair and execution feedback, but optimizing execution success does not necessarily yield strong fault-revealing oracles. This objective, widely adopted in repair-based methods, serves only as a proxy and may be misaligned with the true goal of oracle generation. Such misalignment biases the repair process, giving rise to a feedback-driven degeneration that we term the Self-Repair Trap, where iterative repair progressively drives models toward assertions that are easier to satisfy but less effective at detecting faults. To address this issue, we propose DCAware, a computationally efficient, non-iterative framework that prioritizes high signal-to-noise contextual grounding over multi-round repair. D

translated_title: 逃离自我修复陷阱：通过双上下文感知改进测试预言机生成
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）在回归预言机补全任务中展现出强大潜力，该任务给定测试前缀，并将当前程序版本视为预期行为。近期的方法越来越依赖于迭代式自我修复和执行反馈，但优化执行成功率并不一定能产生具有强故障揭示能力的预言机。这一在基于修复的方法中被广泛采用的目标仅是一个代理指标，可能与预言机生成的真正目标不一致。这种不一致性使修复过程产生偏差，导致一种由反馈驱动的退化现象，我们将其称为“自我修复陷阱”（Self-Repair Trap）：迭代修复逐渐使模型倾向于生成更容易满足但检测故障效果较差的断言。为解决这一问题，我们提出了DCAware，一个计算高效的非迭代框架，它优先采用高信噪比的上下文锚定（contextual grounding），而非多轮修复。
tldr: 针对LLM测试预言机生成中迭代自我修复引发的“自我修复陷阱”——断言越来越容易满足但故障检测能力不断下降，本文提出计算高效的非迭代框架DCAware，通过双上下文感知以高信噪比的上下文锚定取代多轮修复，从而提升预言机的故障揭示能力。
en_tdlr: The paper identifies the "Self-Repair Trap" in LLM-based test oracle generation—where iterative self-repair progressively drives models toward easier-to-satisfy but less fault-revealing assertions—and proposes DCAware, a computationally efficient non-iterative framework that leverages dual-context awareness to prioritize high signal-to-noise contextual grounding over multi-round repair, thereby improving fault-detection effectiveness.
